messages.content: Predict this human bidder’s observed action in a paid laboratory auction. In each of 18 paid periods, you and one randomly rematched human bid against a computer for two items sold sequentially. Both item values are common to all bidders and public. All three current budgets are displayed. A new budget is assigned each period; buying the first item reduces only the winner’s budget for the second item by its sale price. Budgets reset next period; unspent budget earns nothing. Winning an item yields its value minus the price paid; losing costs zero. Profits from all paid periods are added and exchanged at 50 ECU per US dollar, with a USD 5 show-up fee. Accumulated earnings were not displayed during play. Ties are resolved randomly. Do not communicate with other participants. For each item an ascending clock starts at zero and rises about 1 ECU per second. You can click Leave at any time; when a bidder leaves their budget disappears from all screens. A bidder is automatically dropped when the clock reaches their current budget. The computer stays until its remaining budget is reached. The last bidder wins at the last other bidder’s exit price. If the item value is reached, remaining bidders are automatically dropped and a random tied winner pays that value. From the auction-start information, forecast the clock price at this participant’s later recorded voluntary Leave click. This task covers identifiable voluntary exits only; it is not a precommitted maximum bid or a forecast of the entire exit/censoring process. Future within-item updates are not supplied at this forecast origin. Output only that observed exit price in ECU, without an explanation.

Both item values are common to all bidders and public. All three current budgets are displayed. A new budget is assigned each period; buying the first item reduces only the winner’s budget for the second item by its sale price. Budgets reset next period; unspent budget earns nothing. Winning an item yields its value minus the price paid; losing costs zero. Profits from all paid periods are added and exchanged at 50 ECU per US dollar, with a USD 5 show-up fee. Accumulated earnings were not displayed during play. Ties are resolved randomly. Do not communicate with other participants. For each item an ascending clock starts at zero and rises about 1 ECU per second. You can click Leave at any time; when a bidder leaves their budget disappears from all screens. A bidder is automatically dropped when the clock reaches their current budget. The computer stays until its remaining budget is reached. The last bidder wins at the last other bidder’s exit price. If the item value is reached, remaining bidders are automatically dropped and a random tied winner pays that value. From the auction-start information, forecast the clock price at this participant’s later recorded voluntary Leave click. This task covers identifiable voluntary exits only; it is not a precommitted maximum bid or a forecast of the entire exit/censoring process. Future within-item updates are not supplied at this forecast origin. Output only that observed exit price in ECU, without an explanation.

Both item values are common to all bidders and public. All three current budgets are displayed. A new budget is assigned each period; buying the first item reduces only the winner’s budget for the second item by its sale price. Budgets reset next period; unspent budget earns nothing. Winning an item yields its value minus the price paid; losing costs zero. Profits from all paid periods are added and exchanged at 50 ECU per US dollar, with a USD 5 show-up fee. Accumulated earnings were not displayed during play. Ties are resolved randomly. Do not communicate with other participants. For each item an ascending clock starts at zero and rises about 1 ECU per second. You can click Leave at any time; when a bidder leaves their budget disappears from all screens. A bidder is automatically dropped when the clock reaches their current budget. The computer stays until its remaining budget is reached. The last bidder wins at the last other bidder’s exit price. If the item value is reached, remaining bidders are automatically dropped and a random tied winner pays that value. From the auction-start information, forecast the clock price at this participant’s later recorded voluntary Leave click. This task covers identifiable voluntary exits only; it is not a precommitted maximum bid or a forecast of the entire exit/censoring process. Future within-item updates are not supplied at this forecast origin. Output only that observed exit price in ECU, without an explanation.

Both item values are common to all bidders and public. All three current budgets are displayed. A new budget is assigned each period; buying the first item reduces only the winner’s budget for the second item by its sale price. Budgets reset next period; unspent budget earns nothing. Winning an item yields its value minus the price paid; losing costs zero. Profits from all paid periods are added and exchanged at 50 ECU per US dollar, with a USD 5 show-up fee. Accumulated earnings were not displayed during play. Ties are resolved randomly. Do not communicate with other participants. For each item an ascending clock starts at zero and rises about 1 ECU per second. You can click Leave at any time; when a bidder leaves their budget disappears from all screens. A bidder is automatically dropped when the clock reaches their current budget. The computer stays until its remaining budget is reached. The last bidder wins at the last other bidder’s exit price. If the item value is reached, remaining bidders are automatically dropped and a random tied winner pays that value. From the auction-start information, forecast the clock price at this participant’s later recorded voluntary Leave click. This task covers identifiable voluntary exits only; it is not a precommitted maximum bid or a forecast of the entire exit/censoring process. Future within-item updates are not supplied at this forecast origin. Output only that observed exit price in ECU, without an explanation.
